term: conditional necessity, possibility burdens, and scope
resolution: NecessaryIf uses a boxed conditional at one standpoint; a bare actual conditional is strictly insufficient, as the universal Bool control shows. Neither expression instantiates G. The scalar proposition G is distinct from Scott NE and its essence quantification. K5 Euclideanness suffices for both constructive escalations; no minimal-frame or necessity characterization is claimed. Coverage uses the explicit ExcludedMiddle premise. Exclusivity additionally needs an accessible world: empty K5 satisfies both boxes. S5 reflexivity supplies a successor, and its equivalence components permit opposite necessities at disconnected standpoints; no global metaphysical truth is inferred. ◇G and ◇¬G are equally explicit open burdens. Conceivability, failure to derive contradiction, and wording that stipulates possibility do not certify either. Domain-restricted odd-number examples explain a restriction without showing that a proposed divine essence has a model. All models here are mathematical controls, not metaphysical possibilities or source attributions. The separate NecessaryIfConnectivity result proves an exact POINTWISE correspondence only when the forward schema is valid for ALL predicates W→Prop. It does not characterize validity for a single chosen G or a restricted admissible domain. The exact condition is masked successor strong connectivity, strictly weaker than Euclideanness; T+B also suffices. Mathlib ReflTransGen paths use zero or more steps, while Box and Dia still use one-step access; no modal operator is replaced by reachability. Paths ending inside the successor set cannot make an excursion outside it, as restrict_path certifies. Classicality, either possibility burden and the actual/global distinctions retain their original scope.
